steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethnic inequality in employment: ethnic minorities earn less on average. Wood's CV study: identical CVs, 'White' names got 74% more callbacks. This proves discrimination operates in hiring.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Institutional racism (Macpherson Report, 1999): 'the collective failure of an organisation to provide an appropriate service to people because of their colour, culture or ethnic origin'. Found the Met Police was institutionally racist.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethnicity and crime: Black people are 9x more likely to be stopped and searched; 12% of prison vs 3% of population. Self-report studies show similar offending rates - the disparity reflects policing bias.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Islamophobia: prejudice against Muslims increased after 9/11 and 7/7. Muslims face employment discrimination, media stereotyping, and rising hate crime.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain what institutional racism is and evaluate its usefulness. | Describe the evidence for ethnic inequality in employment and crime. | Evaluate whether legislation has effectively reduced ethnic inequality.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Institutional racism: collective failure of an organisation due to race (Macpherson). Found in police, education, CJS. Useful: explains systemic patterns without individual racist intent. Criticism: c | Employment: Wood's CV study proved discrimination (74% more callbacks for White names). Crime: Black people 9x more likely to be stopped; 12% of prison vs 3% of population. Causes: discrimination, ins | Legislation has improved formal equality but discrimination persists (CV studies, stop and search). Legislation addresses individual discrimination but not structural inequality. Conclusion: necessary

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Institutional racism = SYSTEMIC bias (Macpherson/Stephen Lawrence). Not just individual prejudice. Employment: CV study PROVES discrimination (White names = 74% more callbacks). Legislation necessary but NOT sufficient: laws change faster than attitudes and structures.
